objectives.scope: The source’s broad contraindication lists need explicit safety clarification for hepatitis, HIV, HSV, medications, metabolic disease and preterm supplementation. This is decision-oriented teaching, not a drug-specific hold-time or metabolic diet prescription.

visualReview.purpose: Checked Apgar boundaries/table, fetal-shunt diagram, cold-stress figure, scalp compartments, primitive-reflex table, conflicting vital-sign ranges and actual Ballard score-to-age chart.

Checked breast anatomy, all five positions, C/U and scissor holds, asymmetric latch technique, milk-transfer/diaper evaluation and outdated side-by-side storage table. Image-only text was incorporated in the notes.
Confirmed the final worksheet page is blank; no hidden care-plan table or completed patient case is omitted.

emphasis.handling: Exact scoped spans only; no inline Markdown/HTML. All prior CSV decisions and authored additions are unchanged.

materialLimits.handling: No supplied patient case; arithmetic uses the original Apgar table rather than a fabricated case. Resuscitation is referred to trained neonatal protocols.
No complete supplied age/weight percentile case; the actual Ballard chart supplies a 35-point-to-38-week illustration, with size requiring separate percentile plotting.
Source screen/treatment shortcuts are not complete algorithms; no universal glucose threshold, hourly heel-stick plan, bilirubin treatment table or medication-dose table is authored.

The lecture lists conditions without individual diet/drug hold protocols. Current distinctions are clarified; specialist feeding amounts, exposure hold times and metabolic treatment remain individualized.

clarifications.issue: Apgar >100 boundary, one 10-minute repeat and delayed resuscitation implications
clarifications.handling: Use ≥100 for 2 heart-rate points, indicated repeat scoring through 20 minutes, and immediate condition-based care; Apgar alone does not diagnose asphyxia or determine NICU admission.

clarifications.issue: Any respiratory pause <20 seconds labeled normal; single oxygen number applied at birth
clarifications.handling: Interpret effort/color/heart rate and urgent symptoms; avoid routine suction and use the neonatal/CCHD context rather than a single >95% birth target.

clarifications.issue: Molding and caput conflated; subgaleal figure lacks explanatory nursing text
clarifications.handling: Separate skull shape, edema, periosteal and subgaleal bleeding, with progressive swelling/perfusion deterioration urgent.
Differentiate true clunk from click and knee-height comparison from folds; isolated physical traits do not diagnose syndromes.

clarifications.issue: Term 38–42 and fixed gram cutoffs used as SGA/LGA
clarifications.handling: Use standard gestational boundaries and gestational-age percentiles separately from weight.

clarifications.issue: Prophylaxis/screening timing, HBIG series and no-news result tracking
clarifications.handling: Separate purposes/timing, maternal-status/weight-based HBV prevention, multi-disorder screens and confirmed follow-up.

clarifications.issue: Incomplete safe sleep, fever and follow-up teaching
clarifications.handling: Clarify separate firm flat back-sleep surface, urgent fever and early newborn weight/feeding/jaundice review.

clarifications.issue: Fixed early volumes, 10% weight loss treated as automatically normal and nonspecific vitamin advice
clarifications.handling: Do not turn later neonatal values into first-day prescriptions; assess weight/hydration and individualize nutrients including vitamin D.

clarifications.issue: Image-only feeding evaluation omitted by extraction; sleepy/poor intake minimized
clarifications.handling: Include deep latch/transfer cues and age-related diaper trends; assess persistent pain and inadequate intake promptly.

clarifications.issue: Eight-day milk refrigeration and glass-only/container advice
clarifications.handling: Use current CDC milk storage, thawing, leftover and pump-cleaning guidance with hospital high-risk exceptions explicit.

clarifications.issue: Formula four-hour room limit, generalized refrigerator limits and running-tap preparation shortcut
clarifications.handling: Use exact labeled dilution, high-risk newborn water preparation, two-hour/one-hour/24-hour clocks, and no bottle propping.

clarifications.issue: Blanket feeding contraindications for hepatitis/HIV, affected breast HSV, medications and metabolic disease
clarifications.handling: Distinguish direct/expressed milk and affected side, ART/viral status, specific agents, classic galactosemia versus specialist PKU/MSUD plans, and human-milk support for preterm infants.

clarifications.issue: Source limits bilirubin to symptoms and implies later jaundice is always physiologic
clarifications.handling: Document a predischarge measured bilirubin with age/risk-based interpretation and follow-up; avoid the fixed source table and do not dismiss later jaundice.

sharedViews: Six normal-newborn and six feeding answers reuse the existing topic mapping. Transition, head-to-toe assessment, gestational assessment and discharge teaching also appear in Week 10. Static Reader articles are generated from the same content. Original objective order/mappings, PDF files/previews, practice banks/access, videos and navigation remain unchanged.
limits: Source-led educational material, with concise labeled safety clarifications rather than replacement lecture content. Automated checks establish source/text preservation, coverage and rendering; they do not constitute independent clinical validation or a physical iPhone/Safari test.
